computation_method: Cross-sectional rank IC | Monthly | 2012-01 to 2023-12 (144 months, 120 train + 24 val)

direction_alignment.note: Factor DB Z_Score direction-aligned by negating raw Z_Score for ESBR/SUE/AC21_CF. This reproduces Pilot 4 positive IC=+0.0318 from Z_Score_Aligned output of load_month_factors(). C13 compliant.
direction_alignment.verification: IC=+0.03249 from direction-aligned Z_Score exactly matches Pilot 4 IC=+0.0318.

residualization_models.capm_proxy: D10_Blume_Adj_Beta — Blume-adjusted beta from Factor DB. Cross-sectional regressor per month.
residualization_models.ff3_proxy: D10_Blume_Adj_Beta + S01_Size (market cap) + V01_BM (book-to-market). Cross-sectional per month.

pit_compliance.C1: PASS — no full-sample statistics. All computations are monthly cross-sections.
pit_compliance.C2: PASS — fwd_ret = Close(T+1 month-end) / Close(T month-end) - 1. No same-day look-ahead.
pit_compliance.C3: PASS — signal aggregation at T, applied to forward return T+1.
pit_compliance.C13: PASS — Z_Score_Aligned direction respected via corrected direction negation.
pit_compliance.C14: PASS — factor signals use only information at sig_date T.

ff3_residual.interpretation: RAPC signal is largely explained by Size + BM (FF3 factors). After removing all three factors, very little IC remains. RAPC does NOT have FF3-orthogonal alpha as a primary characteristic.
ff3_residual.economic_explanation: Earnings surprise (ESBR/SUE) and accrual (AC21) are empirically correlated with size and value in KR market. The fundamental alpha mechanism (PEAD, accrual anomaly) partially operates through size/value channels. Pure market-neutral component is what CAPM residual captures (97.4% retention).

train_2016_2019.note: FF3 retention negative — FF3 regressor over-explains signal in this period.

subperiod_ic_retention.stability_note: Subperiod_stability=1.0 (all periods positive IC, consistent with Pilot 4). CAPM retention consistently 97% across ALL periods — extremely stable. FF3 retention unstable and near-zero.

crisis_n13.note: CAPM retention drops to 52% in CRISIS. In crash environments, beta becomes unstable (D10_Blume_Adj_Beta noisy) → residualization less reliable. FF3 breaks down entirely. Risk Agent should be aware of this.

bull_n13.note: BULL retention >100% — CAPM residualization slightly enhances IC in rising market. Suggests alpha signal has idiosyncratic component that shines when market noise is removed.

sonnet_vs_opus_delta.reason: Sonnet used CAPM R2 heuristic (raw_ic * sqrt(1-R2)) vs Opus actual cross-sectional IC regression. Heuristic underestimates retention by ~15.9pp.

hedge_compatibility_judgment.critical_caveat: FF3 retention only 10.5% means RAPC alpha is primarily a MARKET-related phenomenon (strong CAPM retention) that ALSO loads on size and value. Hedge against pure market beta (Option A) preserves 97.4% of alpha. But FF3-neutral portfolio would destroy most signal.

bootstrap_ci.note: Wide CI reflects estimation uncertainty from 143 months of IC data. Point estimate is robust (consistent across all subperiods) but tail scenarios (retention<70%) are non-negligible. Risk Agent should use soft constraint, not hard, given this uncertainty.
